ai.description: *Sibynophis collaris* is a slender snake reaching 60–90 cm. It features a dark head with a distinct pale nuchal collar, a brown body with black crossbars, and a yellow-spotted white venter.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Sibynophis collaris* is the distinct, broad black collar on the neck, which is bordered anteriorly by a thin, pale yellow line.
ai.habitat: *Sibynophis collaris* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests across the Himalayas and Western Ghats, typically at elevations ranging from 500 to 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Collared Black-headed Snake is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small lizards and skinks among leaf litter during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Sibynophis collaris* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–6 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with eggs often deposited in moist soil or leaf litter.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Sibynophis collaris* occurs in the Himalayas and Northeast India, ranging from Himachal Pradesh to Arunachal Pradesh at elevations between 500 and 2,500 meters.
